Week 3 Assignment — Programming Logic and Automation

ECN 4199 — Industrial Data Analytics

Assignment Information

Item Details
Week Week 3
Topic Programming Logic and Automation for Economic Analysis
Marks 5 Marks
Duration 1 Hour
Submission Format Google Colab notebook link
Attempts One Attempt Only
Access Lecturer Passcode Required

Assignment Objective

This assignment evaluates whether students can translate economic rules into logical and reusable Python code.

Students must demonstrate:

  • conditional logic
  • boundary testing
  • loops
  • functions
  • integrated automation
  • economic interpretation
  • verification of AI-generated code

Variables, data types, and lists are treated as prior knowledge from Weeks 1 and 2.

Before You Begin

  1. Open the Week 3 live notebook.
  2. Select:
File -> Save a copy in Drive
  1. Rename the notebook:
Week03_IndexNumber_Name.ipynb
  1. Write your name and index number in the first Markdown cell.
  2. Run all completed code cells before submission.

Task 1 — Conditional Logic

Marks: 1

Write a function called:

classify_inflation(inflation)

Use these rules:

Inflation Rate Classification
Below 5 Low inflation
5 to 15, inclusive Moderate inflation
Above 15 High inflation

Your function must return the classification.

Test it using:

test_rates = [4.9, 5, 12, 15, 15.1]

Questions

  1. How is exactly 5 classified?
  2. How is exactly 15 classified?
  3. Why should boundary values be tested?

Task 2 — Loop and Stored Results

Marks: 1

Use:

gdp_growth_rates = [3.5, 5.2, -7.8, 2.1, -1.4]

Create an empty list called:

growth_categories

Use a loop to classify each value:

GDP Growth Classification
Below 0 Recession
0 to below 3 Slow growth
3 or above Strong growth

Store each classification in growth_categories.

Print both the growth value and its classification.

Question

Why is saving results in a list more useful than only printing them?

Task 3 — Reusable Percentage-Change Function

Marks: 1

Create:

percentage_change(old_value, new_value)

Use:

[(new value - old value) / old value] × 100

Apply the function to:

Indicator Old Value New Value
GDP 5000 5400
CPI 200 240
LKR per USD exchange rate 300 330

Round each result to two decimal places.

Write one sentence interpreting each result.

Task 4 — Integrated Automation

Marks: 1

Use:

indicators = ["GDP", "CPI", "Exchange rate"]
old_values = [5000, 200, 300]
new_values = [5400, 240, 330]

Write a loop using:

zip()

For each indicator:

  1. calculate percentage change using your function
  2. print the indicator name
  3. print the rounded result
  4. print a short interpretation label

Suggested labels:

  • GDP: "Economic growth"
  • CPI: "Inflation"
  • Exchange rate: "Currency depreciation"

Question

What parts of this workflow are automated, and what parts still require economic judgement?

Task 5 — Debugging and AI Verification

Marks: 1

An AI tool generated:

def classify_inflation(inflation):
    if inflation < 15:
        return "Low inflation"
    elif inflation < 5:
        return "Moderate inflation"
    else:
        return "High inflation"

Complete all of the following:

  1. Identify the logical error.
  2. Explain why "Moderate inflation" can never be returned.
  3. Correct the function.
  4. Test the corrected function using 4.9, 5, 15, and 15.1.
  5. In 80–120 words, explain why economists must verify AI-generated code.

Submission Checklist

Before submitting, confirm that:

  • all five tasks are complete
  • every code cell has been run
  • output is visible
  • interpretations are written in Markdown cells
  • boundary tests are included
  • the notebook name is correct
  • sharing access is set to:
Anyone with the link -> Viewer

Common Errors

Missing Colon

Wrong:

if inflation < 5

Correct:

if inflation < 5:

Incorrect Indentation

Wrong:

if growth < 0:
print("Recession")

Correct:

if growth < 0:
    print("Recession")

Assignment Instead of Comparison

Wrong:

if status = "Employed":

Correct:

if status == "Employed":

Forgetting return

A function must return a result if that result will be reused.

Academic Integrity

Students may use lecture materials and AI tools for support.

However:

  • copied notebooks are not permitted
  • students must explain all submitted code
  • AI-generated code must be tested and verified
  • interpretations must be written in the student’s own words

Students are responsible for the correctness of all submitted work.
